discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 251823
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
123 PM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Widespread rain develops Thanksgiving afternoon and continues into 
  Friday morning. A few snowflakes may mix in Thursday night. 

- Breezy through Friday with temperatures generally in the upper 30s 
  to mid 40s.

- Another round of rain is likely Sunday into Sunday evening. 
  Precipitation could end as a mix with wet snow.

- Mainly dry and seasonable Monday through Wednesday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 123 PM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

A strong PV anomaly dropping southeast through Missouri will merge 
with a Gulf Coast states upper-level wave over the TN Valley on 
Thursday. The resulting large low pressure center then takes a 
northeast pivot up the western spine of the Appalachians. This 
evolution will eventually bring a soaking rain north into the local 
area late Thursday morning into Thursday afternoon, with periods of 
light-moderate rain persisting within the system deformation zone 
into Thursday night and Friday morning. A solid 0.50" to 1.00" of 
rain appears likely, heaviest along/south of US 24 where heavier 1" 
plus totals remain possible. Higher theta-e air riding up the 
isentropic surfaces should support this blossoming rain shield on 
the northern fringe of this system, with locally heavy rainfall 
rates Thursday PM maximizes in more robust frontogenetic banding. 
Thermals could cool just enough in spots late Thursday night into 
Friday morning for wet snow to mix in. Not expecting accums/impacts 
at this time. 

The upper level pattern will remain active this weekend 
as several faster moving shortwaves track east within aggregate 
troughing over the lower 48. A quick moving, moist-starved shortwave 
takes aim on the lower Great Lakes Saturday morning. The lacking 
moisture and weak forcing with the wave precludes a mentionable PoP 
at this time. A larger scale upper trough and developing sfc 
reflection brings the next good chance for rain Sunday afternoon 
into Sunday evening. There could be enough cold air on the backside 
of the sfc low for precip to end as wet snow, though confidence in 
receiving snow is very low. 

A flatter, more zonal flow regime looks to settle in for the first 
half of next week with dry conditions and gradual moderation.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 1137 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

Visible satellite imagery and observations show mid to high
level clouds streaming in from the south ahead of our next 
weather system. VFR conditions will prevail through much of the 
the TAF forecast period. Winds will remain out of the east-
northeast between 10 to 15 kts today and tonight with occasional
gusts to 20 to 25 kts. Dry conditions continue overnight before
rain will overspread the area from SE to NW late Thursday
morning. Have opted to leave out any mention of rain or MVFR/IFR
conditions in the TAFs for now and will let future shifts
assess this potential as more confidence is gained.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 7 AM Thursday to 4 AM EST Saturday 
     for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Steinwedel
AVIATION...Johnson

spc.text:
SPC AC 251947

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0147 PM CST Wed Nov 25 2026

   Valid 252000Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   SOUTH FLORIDA AND THE KEYS AND OVER PORTIONS OF THE COASTAL
   CAROLINAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   An isolated severe threat may develop over south Florida and the
   Keys through this evening, and across parts of the coastal Carolinas
   late tonight.

   ...20z Update...
   Latest observational data continues to depict a convectively
   reinforced baroclinic zone draped across the Florida Straits
   northeastward offshore between Miami, FL, and the Bahamas, with
   minimal inland progression noted over the past several hours.
   Northeasterly low-level flow across much of the Florida Peninsula
   along with persistent cloud cover and stratiform precipitation
   across far south Florida continue to limit buoyancy over land
   (reference the 18z MFL observed sounding). Given this, confidence
   continues to increase that stronger convective development will
   remain offshore of the southeast Florida coast/Upper Keys through
   the rest of the afternoon/evening. Thus, the Level 2/Slight risk and
   corresponding 5% tornado probabilities across south Florida have
   been dropped with this outlook update, and the Level 1/Marginal Risk
   (and associated low tornado/wind probabilities) have been trimmed
   southward.

   Elsewhere, the general thunder area across portions of the central
   Gulf Coast has been trimmed in the wake of prior convection that has
   shifted eastward in tandem with a surface trough and mid/upper
   shortwave.

   ..Chalmers/Gleason.. 11/25/2026

   .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1030 AM CST Wed Nov 25 2026/

   ...Central Gulf Coast into South Florida and the Keys...
   The lead/southern mid-level trough centered over the ArkLaTex/lower
   MS Valley late this morning will translate eastward today while
   becoming absorbed into a broader upper trough/low expected to
   develop over the Southeast/Mid-South through the period. Ongoing
   strong convection over the nearshore waters of the northern Gulf
   (south of Gulf Shores AL/Pensacola FL) will struggle to advance
   inland due to strong surface ridging and minimal instability
   persisting over land. Additional convection may approach the
   west-central FL Coast later this afternoon/evening, but with the
   same thermodynamic limitations.

   A separate zone of stratiform precipitation is occurring across
   south FL and the Keys in association with a weak mid-level
   perturbation and warm advection occurring generally along/north of a
   convectively reinforced baroclinic zone draped across the FL Straits
   northeastward offshore between Miami FL and the Bahamas. Most
   short-term guidance continues to suggest that a weak surface low
   will attempt to develop near this front and track northeastward
   along/near the southeast FL Coast through the afternoon. Given
   ongoing precipitation and widespread cloudiness, it remains
   uncertain whether greater low-level moisture (mid/upper 70s) surface
   dewpoints will be able to appreciably advance inland. If they do,
   then this could potentially help offset poor lapse rates and the
   saturated profile noted in the observed 12Z KEY sounding.

   Still, based on the latest observations trends, there is probably a
   greater chance (more than 50%) that stronger convection will develop
   just offshore from the southeast FL Coast and adjacent Upper Keys
   this afternoon. Will maintain the Slight Risk for the isolated
   tornado potential given the presence of otherwise favorable
   low-level shear, but the threat over land appears rather conditional
   at this time.

   ...Coastal Carolinas...
   The surface low forecast to develop off the FL Atlantic Coast this
   afternoon will move northward and deepen over the Gulf Stream before
   eventually moving inland along the NC/SC Coast early Thursday
   morning (around 26/09-12Z). Uncertainty remains high regarding
   inland destabilization, but a narrow moist sector may overspread the
   Outer Banks/coastal NC late tonight into early Thursday morning.
   While instability will likely remain quite weak per recent RAP/HRRR
   forecast soundings, strengthening low-level wind fields could
   support the potential for organized convection capable of producing
   isolated severe gusts and perhaps a tornado.

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0100Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 251720

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1120 AM CST Wed Nov 25 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER EASTERN
   NORTH CAROLINA INTO PORTIONS OF EASTERN VIRGINIA AND SOUTHEAST
   MARYLAND...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe storms capable of damaging winds and perhaps a brief
   tornado appear possible over eastern North Carolina into portions of
   eastern Virginia and southeast Maryland on Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...

   A negatively tilted short-wave trough is forecast to lift north
   along the Atlantic Coast in advance of an intense mid/upper-level
   low, which will progress from the Mid-South into the central
   Appalachians. In the low levels, a surface cyclone initially over
   eastern NC at 12Z Thursday will undergo occlusion while developing
   into the upper OH Valley. A weaker, secondary cyclone may develop
   along a baroclinic zone along or just offshore of the Mid-Atlantic
   coast Thursday afternoon, with that feature tracking along the New
   England coast Thursday evening into Thursday night.  

   Elsewhere, a short-wave trough and associated mid/upper-level wind
   maxima will advance from the vicinity of the Pacific Northwest and
   BC coasts along the international border into the northern Plains
   and SK/MB by 12Z Friday. 


   ...Eastern North Carolina to Southern New England...

   Strong low-level warm advection and midlevel height falls preceding
   the lead upper-air disturbance will contribute to at least isolated
   thunderstorms embedded within a broader precipitation shield lifting
   north through the Mid-Atlantic into southern New England. The
   majority of the storms will likely be elevated atop a stable,
   near-surface inversion and rooted within a marginally unstable,
   weak-lapse-rate environment. However, a few surface-based storms
   appear possible on the southern flank of the precipitation shield
   from eastern NC into the VA/MD Tidewater region Thursday, where 12Z
   REFS guidance indicates a relatively narrow corridor of weak
   surface-based instability (e.g., SBCAPE of 250-500 J/kg). 

   Veering winds with height with sufficient low-level and deep-layer
   shear will conditionally support some marginal/transient supercell
   potential with an associated risk for isolated damaging wind
   occurrences and/or a brief tornado or waterspout. As such, 5-percent
   wind and 2-percent tornado probabilities have been included with
   this forecast update.


   ...Pacific Northwest...

   Moist, onshore flow in the low levels will coincide with dynamic
   cooling aloft to yield air mass destabilization over western WA
   Thursday morning with MLCAPE increasing to a few hundred J/kg.
   Widely scattered thunderstorms are likely to move onshore at that
   time within the zone of strongest forcing for ascent attendant to
   the short-wave trough. Downdraft-aided turbulent mixing of stronger
   flow aloft could yield a few strong wind gusts, especially at higher
   elevations. Some small hail may also occur owing to the presence of
   relatively steep lapse rates and cool midlevel temperatures.

   ..Mead.. 11/25/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 251858

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1258 PM CST Wed Nov 25 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are unlikely on Friday through Friday night.

   ...Synopsis and Discussion...

   An intense deep-layer cyclone over the central Appalachians into the
   upper OH Valley at 12Z Friday will move into New England ahead of a
   short-wave trough progressing from the northern Plains into the
   Great Lakes. A separate short-wave trough and associated
   mid/upper-level jet streaks will move onto the Pacific Northwest
   coast Friday and into portions of the Interior West Friday night
   into early Saturday. Forcing for ascent and related steepening of
   midlevel lapse rates preceding that disturbance may be sufficient to
   support a few lightning strikes from the vicinity of the OR coast
   toward the Snake River Valley and northern Great Basin. However,
   expected coverage is too sparse to include a general thunderstorm
   area. Across the remainder of the CONUS, dry and stable conditions
   will preclude thunderstorm development.

   ..Mead.. 11/25/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
